title: Agentic engineering — check what stuck
intro: Nine self-check questions written from the course labs (no official quiz exists).

questions.prompt: The week-1 pattern for accuracy-critical work is…
choices: One strong model, carefully prompted
Parallel generation from several models, with an evaluator/picker choosing the best
Always using the largest local model
Retrying the same prompt until it looks right
questions.explanation: Send the task to multiple models, judge the candidates — the lab's own commercial note: universal where accuracy is critical.

questions.prompt: In the Agents SDK, a handoff differs from a tool because…
choices: Handoffs are faster
Control transfers: the receiving agent takes over the conversation, instead of returning a result to the caller
Tools can only be Python functions
Handoffs don't appear in traces
questions.explanation: Tool = consultation (caller stays in charge); handoff = delegation of the whole conversation to a specialist.

choices: Makes the agent's answers longer
Judges the request and can trip BEFORE the expensive pipeline runs
Replaces the need for traces
Caches previous runs
questions.explanation: A guardrail agent returns GuardrailFunctionOutput on the input — blocking bad runs before money is spent, not after.

questions.prompt: In CrewAI, an agent is defined by…
choices: A graph node and reducer
role, goal, backstory (and model) in agents.yaml
A message handler registered with a runtime
A handoff_description
questions.explanation: Crews are org charts: people in agents.yaml, work in tasks.yaml, process in crew.py. Backstories are prompt engineering with a personnel file.

choices: A smaller language model
The function (named via Annotated) that merges a node's update into the State
A tool that compresses context
The final node in every graph
questions.explanation: State fields declare how updates combine — add_messages for the common case. Reducers make concurrent updates principled.

questions.prompt: LangGraph's checkpointing (the labs' memory.db) buys you…
choices: Faster model inference
Resume, replay and persistence per step — the graph remembers where it was
Automatic prompt optimization
Free hosting
questions.explanation: A SQLite checkpointer persists state at each step — crash recovery and time-travel debugging for long-running flows.

choices: Agents must all use the same model
Decoupling an agent's logic from how messages are delivered — a Runtime owns delivery and lifecycle
Replacing Python with JavaScript
Running only in distributed mode
questions.explanation: Core is a framework-agnostic interaction layer: agents do their work; the runtime owns transport — in-process today, distributed tomorrow.

questions.prompt: Equipping an SDK agent with MCP tools takes three moves:
choices: Fork the server, edit its code, redeploy
Create a client, have it spawn the server, collect the tools
Write JSON schemas for each tool by hand
Fine-tune the model on the tool docs
questions.explanation: Client → spawn → collect, then hand the tools to an Agent like any others. Capability assembly at config speed.

questions.prompt: In the Autonomous Traders capstone, a trader's investment strategy lives…
choices: Hardcoded in the trader's prompt
As an MCP resource the agent reads — versioned instructions, separate from tools
Inside the buy/sell tool code
In the model's weights
questions.explanation: State and instructions are resources; actions are tools. One accounts server serves four traders, and swapping a brain never touches the money logic.
